notes: New stored edit (very_unlikely), replacing "e^iπ equals 1": two models missed its direct question (Llama answered "i-1", Mistral "Euler's formula"), and the notation itself confused them. The square of i is the defining fact of the imaginary unit. Mathematics leaves out worlds and the indeterminate query (README, Shape per topic): a fact about a number, a shape or a proof rests on definitions, so the edit leaves no consistent world to split between; the record has 4 determinate derived queries. Derived queries ask what the edit forces with the definitions held fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. The relation has_square is functional (near: is it still −1?) and chains through equality (has_square ∘ equals ⊑ has_square). Three derived queries have the same form, whether the square of i equals a quantity that is 1 (the cosine of 0, the Earth's natural satellites, the atomic number of hydrogen), so all three are labelled chain, task answer. The fourth subtracts 1 (derivation none, task composition with the stored fact 1 minus 1 is 0: arithmetic, not a step in the has_square chain). The far query reaches the imaginary unit by its engineering name j (binding): "j^2 = -1" is written out in engineering texts, so its answer is stored under that name and must move from -1 to 1; the j convention is its bridge and has a check. It replaced "What is i cubed?", whose answer (-i before, i after) contains the letter the question names. Expected answers: criteria.py's normaliser drops punctuation, so "-1" and "1" would read as the same answer. The original answer of the direct, paraphrase and cross-lingual questions and of the far query is therefore written "negative 1" (the new answer is "1"); the edit text and yes/no queries keep the minus sign U+2212. New relation has_square is in staging.
